analysis.title: A Year After Saying "Short Hyperscaler Bonds", Hartnett Now Says Buy Them
key_insights: Hartnett's Biggest Picture call: buy tech bond 'diamonds in the rough'. US tech bonds are down 9% YTD and their return relative to the IG index is at a 30-year low. A year ago he said to short hyperscaler bonds.

Hyperscaler debt issuance rose to $182bn in 2026 from $17bn in 2024. Mag7-style bond yields are 6-8% (Table 1): Meta 2066s 7.40%, Oracle 2066s 8.43%, CoreWeave 2031s 14.26%. Microsoft and Apple long bonds pay above 6%.

Hyperscaler equity issuance reached $89bn in 2026, so new paper (bonds plus stock) is $271bn YTD. Hyperscaler buybacks run at $14bn annualized YTD vs $105bn in 2024, and Hartnett says the era of big buybacks is over.

Meta launched an equity raise of up to $95bn: a $35bn offering of common and mandatory convertible preferred, plus an at-the-market program of up to $60bn of non-voting Class C shares. Hartnett reads it as new respect for credit investors, since equity sits below bonds in the capital structure.

Hyperscaler spreads have not peaked yet. IG spreads widened toward recent wides by Thursday, data center CDS widened, and Meta's Beignet SPV bonds sold off. Microsoft asked for at least $25bn in its first dollar bond deal since 2017. The Durden commentary says the bonds may need more equity deals before the peak.

Super trends framework: ABB (Anything but Bonds), ABC (Anywhere but China), ABD (Anything but Dollar) and AI. The AI Big 10 is 41% of US market cap. In the 2020s, annualized returns are -4% for the 10Y Treasury, -5% for China stocks (HSCEI), 15% for gold and 17% for the Nasdaq.

ABB and AI now collide. Populist politics keep allocators underweight bonds and positioned for a steeper yield curve, while higher yields hurt the AI stock bull because bond markets fund hyperscaler capex ($240bn in 2024 to a free cash flow of -$180bn in 2027E). Hartnett expects YCC/QE threat to cap yields, with the release valve in H1'27 from geopolitical peace, a big drop in oil and an end of rate hikes.

Hartnett is tactically cautious on the tape: 42 global central bank hikes in the past six months, US dollar and UST yields up for four months, tech leadership stalling (NDX 30k cap, SOX -20%). He calls it 'classic painful tightening stuff but not mortal unless job losses/credit event'. Next big risk-on move awaits the end of hikes and an oil collapse in H1'27.

Key levels to hold before a year-end rally: MAGS $70 and SMH $520. MAGS closed at $69.70 Thursday and $68.48 Friday, so the level is already broken. SMH closed at $522.49 Friday after a low of $511.63.

Political call: a Democratic sweep is mostly priced as risk-off, but a Democratic wave (+53 Senate seats) and a jump in bond yields are not. Hartnett says voters want 'affordability', which is negative for tech, bank and energy monopolies in 2027 and positive for consumer discretionary. Polymarket gives Democrats 98% to flip North Carolina and 70% each in Ohio, Alaska and Texas.

China: Hartnett presents both sides on China deflation. New-low China bond yields, CNY up more than 20% vs the Taiwan dollar and CQQQ -32% since June argue it is a global problem. China financials doubling in three years argue it is not. He favors short oil in H1'27, and if lower oil does not trigger a euro and yen bounce, that is the tell that China deflation is a global negative.

Flows for the week through Wednesday: $56.2bn to stocks, $15.4bn to bonds, $3.4bn to cash, $0.5bn out of crypto, $1.7bn out of gold. Gold had its first outflow since July, Japan its biggest inflow since May 2013 ($6.8bn), China its biggest since April 2025 ($25.7bn), and Europe its biggest outflow since July ($2.3bn).

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.1 (from 7.2), neutral since falling below 8.0 in mid-October. Breadth is the only bearish component (21st percentile), FMS positioning is at the 100th percentile and equity flows at the 89th. FMS Cash Rule is on 'sell' at 3.9% and the EM Flow Trading Rule on 'sell' at 2.8%.

YTD scoreboard: oil 79.1%, US stocks 12.7%, global stocks 9.6%, US dollar 3.7%, cash 3.1%, HY -0.5%, IG -2.5%, govt bonds -3.3%, gold -7.1%, bitcoin -8.4%. Gold broke below $4,000 to a one-year low, and bitcoin hit a six-week low after North Korea was blamed for a $6.3bn Binance theft.

trade_ideas.description: Buy US tech (hyperscaler) investment-grade bonds, the 'diamonds in the rough'
trade_ideas.rationale: Tech bonds are down 9% YTD, relative returns to IG are at a 30-year low, and Mag7-style yields are 6-8%.
trade_ideas.risk: Further hyperscaler issuance and widening spreads. The Durden commentary says spreads have not peaked.

trade_ideas.description: Short oil in H1'27 as peace boosts supply

tension_points.bull_case: Tech bonds are down 9% YTD, relative returns are at 30-year lows, yields are 6-8%, and Meta's equity raise shows respect for creditors (equity sits below bonds).
tension_points.bear_case: IG spreads are widening, data center CDS is near wides, Microsoft needed $25bn of bonds, and $4.1 trillion of off-balance sheet obligations remain. The commentary says the peak in spreads likely comes after this week.
tension_points.what_invalidates: MAGS below $70 (already broken) and SMH below $520 (about $2.50 away at Friday's close).

tension_points.bull_case: China is not a global problem: China financials have doubled in three years.
tension_points.bear_case: New-low China bond yields, CNY up more than 20% vs the Taiwan dollar and CQQQ down 32% since June point to deflation exported globally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If lower oil in H1'27 does not trigger a euro and yen bounce, China deflation is a new global negative.

tension_points.bull_case: Policymakers will not allow a disorderly rise in yields, so the YCC/QE threat will cap bond yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Capping yields is not the same as cutting them, and AI needs lower yields to ease financial conditions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The release valve is expected in H1'27 from peace, a collapse in oil and an end of rate hikes.
